page: Amazon Web Services m5d.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance is equipped with 2400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps. No GPUs are present on this server.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores all placing in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is strong, ranking in the top 25% for both read and write operations, though small-block cached reads remain average. Cryptographic and extended instruction capabilities are also strong, supported by hardware-level AVX and AVX-512 flags.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the m5d.16xlarge is defined by its balanced resource density and the inclusion of high-capacity local NVMe storage, which reduces the need for external block storage for temporary data. However, a notable tradeoff is the poor single-threaded execution speed and weak performance in text generation tasks, such as LLM inference where text generation for a 135M model falls into the bottom 10%. This instance is suited for multi-threaded workloads, database operations, static web serving, and applications requiring high local storage throughput rather than raw single-core compute power.
